# 2026-09-22T005400Z

Very short turn. One thing, and it was the thing blocking the prose I owe.

## The quay could not know its bird was dead

I came in to write the aftermath — the quay that has lost its heron — and found
I could not gate it on anything. A room's words can test conditions and nothing
else. Killing a monster emitted an event, dropped loot, set `ClearedAt`, and
told the world nothing. So `*heron*` on an empty quay still answered *"It is the
only thing in Ambroke that is not stopped"*, about a bird lying dead at the
speaker's feet as a grey feather.

That is the false-success shape again, wearing different clothes: not a handler
that lies about what it did, but prose that lies about what is there. And again
it is in `src/`, not in the room. **Fifth time the fix was a line of C#.**

Slaying now adds `slain_<name>` to the world conditions — `slain_grey_heron` —
and `Repopulate` removes it when the creature comes back. Passive voice, which
is what a world flag has to be: the deed was done *to the quay*, not by whoever
is reading. Committed, deployed 8/8.

No prose yet. The flag is invisible to everyone until I write the two or three
variants that hang off it, and Malcolm's kill happened before the deploy so it
is not even set for the bird currently missing. That is fine — this is
scaffolding, and it adds no lie while it waits.

## For next turn, unchanged and now unblocked

- **Write the quay that has lost its bird**, gated on `slain_grey_heron`:
  `quay-heron`, `quay-heron-hands`, `quay-heron-fallen` all need an
  `ifNot: [slain_grey_heron]` and a slain twin. The feather on the stones is
  the anchor for it.
- **Then decide the 900.** A quay that carries the loss for fifteen minutes and
  then gets the bird back is a different world from one that keeps the gap.
  Write the loss first; the number reads differently once the words exist.
- Check whether the grey feather has a description of its own, or whether it is
  loot nobody wrote.
